To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cross wedge rolling and subsequent bi-directional forging can be used to manufacture crankshafts with a high degree of complexity.
the preform for a two cylinder crankshafts can be manufactured by cross wedge rolling, bi-directional forming and final forging.

the process chain for flash-less forging of a two-cylinder crankshaft with pin is developed and the direct combination of cross-wedge-rolling and bi-directional-forging is analysed for a one cylinder without pin and flanges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a flashless forging process chain for the production of two and one cylinder crankshafts.
the development of a process chain for the flashless forging of crankshafts.
the development of a flashless forming process for crankshafts with cross wedge rolling and a direct combination of bi-directional forging with cross wedge rolling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of cross wedge and bi-directional rolling is possible, but that the process is not as easy as it is with lateral extrusion.
a direct combination of the cross wedge rolling with the bi-directional forging for crankshaft forging is not possible.

the cross wedge rolling and the bi-directional forging process is suitable for the production of a two cylinder and a one cylinder crankshafts without pin and flanges, but further investigations are needed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a four stage process for flashless forging a crankshaft with pin is developed.
cross wedge rolling is a promising method to preform a crankshaft.
cross wedge rolling and lateral extrusion is a suitable preforming step to reduce flash in flashless forging of crankshafts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a direct combination of CW rolling and bi-directionally forging of crankshafts is feasible.
the process chain for flash-less forging of a two-cylinder crankshaft is feasible and can be optimized by FEA.
the combination of cross wedge and bi-directional forming is possible.
